summary: This script sets up a basic todo list database with an API schema, creates a todos table with sample data, and configures two database roles with specific permissions—a read-only anonymous user role and an authenticator role that can switch into it. This is a typical pattern for securing a PostgREST API where external requests come in as the limited web_anon user.

explanations.4: Serial means the database auto-increments this number each time you insert a new row, so you don't have to provide an id yourself.
explanations.5: The 'default false' means if you don't specify whether a todo is done when creating it, it automatically becomes false.
explanations.7: Timestamptz is a timestamp that includes timezone information, so it knows exactly what moment in time you mean regardless of where you are in the world.
explanations.13: Nologin means this role can't directly log into the database—it's just a container for permissions that other roles can use.
explanations.18: Login means this role can actually connect to the database, and noinherit means it won't automatically have permissions unless explicitly granted; password sets what you'd use to connect.
explanations.19: This grants the authenticator role membership in web_anon, so authenticator can act as web_anon and use its limited permissions.
